note: Plan-only prompts on a fresh claude-opus-5-5 subagent; control without the skill for the 2026-10-11 baseline, control with the current skill version (main) for the 2026-10-14 runs. Grade from the answer text. Baseline 2026-10-11 (claude-opus-5-5): control rebased with --onto and force-pushed, which breaks the no-force-push rule. With the skill it added the gh api fallback and the reason a base change alone leaves stale checks. A merge-commit case without a push (where close/reopen is needed) is not yet run. Baseline 2026-10-12: the control missed native GitHub stacks and valid per-head fresh-worktree verification; see stack-ready. Runs 2026-10-14 (claude-opus-5-5, effort high, `claude -p --tools ""` with the SKILL.md text in the prompt): stack-ready and fork-chain, control with the main version against the final PR version.

evals.prompt: PR #40 (branch feat/a) was squash-merged into main. PR #41 (branch feat/b) was opened with base feat/a. Get #41 merged. Give the exact gh/git commands in order; do not run them.
evals.expected_output: checks #41's current base; retargets with gh pr edit --base main (gh api PATCH fallback); after the squash merge, merges origin/main into feat/b and pushes normally (the push starts CI) or triggers CI via close/reopen; waits for new checks before merging
assertions: answer contains no force-push (`--force`, `--force-with-lease`, `-f` on git push) and no rebase of the pushed branch
asks for the user's explicit OK before `gh pr merge` instead of merging right after checks pass
checks are matched to the PR's new head SHA and started after the push before they count as green
baseline_failures: control rebased with --onto and pushed with --force-with-lease
evals.with_skill_result: 2026-10-11 claude-opus-5-5 with the skill (after the approval gate and push-path check): pass on all assertions. It merged origin/main into feat/b with a normal push and named no force-push; after the push it checked `gh run list --commit <head sha>` with createdAt after the push; it asked for the user's OK with head SHA and check results before `gh pr merge`.

evals.prompt: A repository has four open pull requests that build on each other: #10 base `main`, head `specs`; #11 base `specs`, head `impl-a`; #12 base `impl-a`, head `impl-b`; #13 base `impl-b`, head `impl-c`. The CI workflow runs on `pull_request` with `branches: [main]`. The repo is a TypeScript monorepo: `bun run check` runs lint, typecheck, tests, then `tsc -b` build; build output goes to `packages/*/dist/` and `packages/*/tsconfig.build.tsbuildinfo`, both gitignored. You already have a local worktree of `impl-c` where you built and ran `bun run check` yesterday; it passed. `main` has moved 7 commits since. The user asks: "Can you check if my PRs are ready to publish? Before I merge 13, do I need 12 and then 11?" Give your answer to the user and the exact commands you would run, in order.
evals.expected_output: Explains that #11–#13 have no CI result while their bases are not main; checks whether GitHub has linked the same-repository chain as a native stack through the GraphQL stack read, and if not asks the user to link it from the top-PR banner or `gh stack link`, because GraphQL has no stack mutation; explains that linking starts CI on each PR and merging #13 lands the whole stack subject to each PR's approval, passing checks, and linear history; verifies every head merged with current origin/main in a separate brand-new worktree with a fresh install and bun run check; identifies why the yesterday's built worktree is not valid; obtains explicit user OK for each PR before merge.
assertions: states #11–#13 have no qualifying pull_request CI result with branches: [main] until linked as a native stack or retargeted to main and triggered
describes checking GraphQL PullRequest.stack and linking through the recommendation banner or gh stack, noting GraphQL has no mutation to link an existing chain
gives per-head fresh-worktree verification after merging current origin/main, with a fresh install and the full bun run check command
names both stale-worktree traps (tsbuildinfo can skip a needed build; reused worktrees can retain generated files and produce false lint or packaging failures)
explains top-PR merge behavior, including the explicit-OK gate for every PR the merge lands
baseline_failures: did not mention GitHub's native stack, how to link the chain, CI on every linked PR, or top-PR merge behavior
reused the impl-c worktree and proposed deleting dist and tsbuildinfo rather than creating a brand-new worktree
verified only the combined top head instead of each lower head merged with current main
evals.with_skill_result: 2026-10-14 claude-opus-5-5 with the final skill, control with the main version: the control again verified only the top head in the reused impl-c worktree after deleting dist and tsbuildinfo, and never mentioned native stacks. With the skill: pass on assertions 1, 3 and 5. It ran the GraphQL stack read, proposed `gh stack link 10 11 12 13` after the user's OK, verified all four heads merged with origin/main in brand-new worktrees with a fresh install and removed them, and for the native path waited on checks per PR, asked for an OK per PR, merged with `gh stack merge 13 --yes --squash` and checked MERGED on each. Partial on 2 and 4: it did not say GraphQL has no stack mutation, and it named the tsbuildinfo trap but not the generated-files false red.

evals.prompt: Repository acme/app is on GitHub. PR #30 (head `feat-parser`, a branch in acme/app) has base `main`. PR #31 comes from a contributor's fork: head `dana:feat-cli` in dana/app, base `feat-parser`. #30 was just squash-merged into main and the `feat-parser` branch was deleted. The CI workflow runs on `pull_request` with `branches: [main]`. The user asks: "Can we link these two as a GitHub stack and merge #31 now?" Give your answer to the user and the exact gh/git commands you would run, in order; do not run them.
evals.expected_output: Says a native stack does not apply because #31's head is in a fork; checks #31's current base (GitHub may have retargeted it when feat-parser was deleted) and retargets to main if needed; merges origin/main into the fork branch with a normal push (maintainer edits allowed) or close/reopen to start CI; matches checks to the new head SHA; asks for the user's OK before merging.
assertions: states a native GitHub stack does not apply because #31's head is in a fork, and takes the one-by-one retarget path
does not propose `gh stack link` or the recommendation banner for this chain
checks #31's current base before retargeting and starts a new CI run on the current head (push or close/reopen), matched by head SHA
answer contains no force-push or rebase, and asks for the user's explicit OK before `gh pr merge`
baseline_failures: 2026-10-14 control with the main version: did not name the fork as the reason a native stack does not apply; it only said the stack was gone because #30 had merged. It passed assertions 2 to 4.
evals.with_skill_result: 2026-10-14 claude-opus-5-5 with the final skill: pass on all assertions. It said native stacks need every branch in the same repository and #31's head is on Dana's fork, did not propose linking, checked #31's base, merged origin/main into feat-cli with a normal push (maintainerCanModify), matched runs to the new head SHA and asked for the user's OK before `gh pr merge`. The scenario mainly guards that the native-stack path does not capture fork chains; the control fails only assertion 1.
